notes: Styling system: a single hand-written stylesheet (styles.css) with CSS custom properties in :root (colour, font, four text sizes, a 4-48 px spacing scale, one radius, one feedback duration). No component library and no build step: five static HTML pages (index, berths, boat, review, confirmed) sharing one IIFE (app.js) that switches on body[data-page]. Stay details travel in the query string between pages. The packet's lint.json and census.json were empty ([] / {}) and design.md was empty, so token drift was checked by reading styles.css directly: every colour, font size, spacing value, radius and duration in component rules resolves to a token; remaining literals are structural (1-3 px borders/outlines, 44 px target minimums, rem max-widths, unitless line heights) and are not drift. No positive tabindex, no down-event activation, no single-key shortcuts, no drag interactions, no text-input key handlers (so no IME hazard), no images. Observed but not raised as findings: the booking is never submitted anywhere (confirmed.html derives a reference 'SQ-MMDD-<berth>' client-side, app.js:237, so two bookings of the same berth and date get the same reference); the More options disclosure (app.js:134-149) does not close when focus leaves it, which the disclosure pattern does not require. No builder notes or other evaluators' outputs were read; .eval/ was not read.

passes.summary: Read all five HTML pages, styles.css and app.js in full; mapped tokens, states, semantics, keyboard model, localisation and motion.

not_assessable: Census-based drift ranking: census.json in the packet was empty, so drift was checked by reading styles.css rather than from computed-style counts.
uie lint output: lint.json in the packet was empty; no static tool findings to cross-check.

strengths.title: Token discipline: every colour, type size, spacing step, radius and transition duration in component rules uses a :root custom property
strengths.evidence: styles.css:3-40 and all component rules; no literal hex colours outside :root

strengths.title: Global focus-visible indicator (3 px solid ink outline, 2 px offset) distinct from hover, with no outline:none anywhere
Reduced-motion path present and transitions limited to colour/background/border properties
Error summary pattern: role=alert container focused on submit, per-field messages wired with aria-invalid and aria-describedby, hints preserved
Contact fields carry autocomplete=name and autocomplete=tel; 44 px minimum targets on buttons, inputs, nav and menu links

candidates.title: Boat details form is emptied every time the page is shown, including after Back from the review page
candidates.description: Details a skipper has entered should survive returning to a step. app.js registers a pageshow listener on the boat page that calls boatForm.reset() (app.js:164-167); pageshow fires on first load and on back/forward-cache restore, so going Back from review.html clears boat name, length, draught and MMSI. The boat page also never prefills from the boat/loa/draught/mmsi query parameters that review.html receives, unlike the plan page which prefills from params (app.js:107-109). The form additionally sets autocomplete="off" (boat.html:42), so the browser cannot offer the values again.
candidates.impact: A skipper who goes back to correct one detail (for example after seeing the total on review) may have to re-enter all four boat fields, including the 9-digit MMSI.

evidence.detail: window.addEventListener('pageshow', function () { boatForm.reset(); }); with comment 'The form is emptied whenever the page is shown, including after the browser's Back button.'
no read of params boat/loa/draught/mmsi into the boat inputs

factor_notes.frequency: Every Back navigation onto the boat step, in both declared journeys that pass through it.
factor_notes.impact: All four fields must be re-typed; no data lost beyond this form.
factor_notes.persistence: Recurs on every return to the step.

candidates.recommendation: Remove the pageshow reset, prefill the inputs from the query parameters when present, and drop autocomplete="off".

candidates.title: Over-length boat leads to a 'Booking stopped' screen that gives no cause and no way to continue
candidates.description: A blocking error should say what went wrong and how to recover. When the entered length exceeds the chosen berth's maximum (app.js:187), the script hides the form and reveals a hard-coded block reading 'Booking stopped' / 'This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' (boat.html:70-73). It does not mention the length limit, the chosen berth, or that a larger berth exists (Wall berth 2 takes up to 15 m, app.js:7), and it offers no link back to the berth choice or the form; the only route on is the masthead or browser Back.

criteria.name: Help users recognize, diagnose, and recover from errors

candidates.impact: A skipper whose boat is longer than the berth they picked may not learn why the booking stopped and may abandon it, although a suitable berth is available.

evidence.detail: if (Number(v('loa')) > berth.max) { boat-step hidden; dead-end shown; focus stopped-title; return; }
static text 'This booking cannot continue. Reference BK-409.' with no link or cause

factor_notes.frequency: Any skipper whose boat exceeds the chosen berth's limit; berths.html lists limits but length is not asked until the next step.
factor_notes.impact: The booking cannot be completed from this screen; recovery requires guessing to go back two steps.
factor_notes.persistence: Recurs whenever the mismatch happens; once understood, users may pick a larger berth.

candidates.recommendation: Treat the mismatch as a field error on Length that names the berth's maximum, and link back to berths.html with the stay query so a larger berth can be chosen.

candidates.title: Error-summary link for the berth choice points at the fieldset, not at a radio button
candidates.description: Error-summary links should move focus to the field to fix. errorKit builds each link as href='#'+fieldId (app.js:80); for the berth error the id is the fieldset 'berth' (berths.html:60). A fieldset is not focusable, so activating the link scrolls but leaves keyboard focus on the link rather than on the first radio, and screen-reader users are not taken into the group.
candidates.impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users may have to search for the berth options after following the error link.

locations.snippet: Choose a pontoon space for your boat

evidence.detail: a.href = '#' + p[0]; for p[0] === 'berth' the target is <fieldset id="berth">

factor_notes.frequency: Only when Continue is pressed with no berth chosen.
factor_notes.impact: Extra navigation to reach the radios; no data lost.

candidates.recommendation: For fieldset targets, link to (or focus on click) the first radio in the group.

candidates.title: Invalid-state border is styled for text inputs only, not for the arrival-time select or the berth radios
candidates.description: Fields in error should carry a consistent visual error state. The only invalid rule is input[aria-invalid="true"] { border-color: var(--color-error) } (styles.css:283-285). app.js sets aria-invalid on the arrival-time <select> (index.html:62) and on the berth radios, but no rule targets select[aria-invalid] or the .option card, so those fields keep their resting border when in error while text inputs turn red.
candidates.impact: In the error state the field needing attention may be less easy to spot on the plan and berth pages than on the boat and contact pages; the error text above the field is still shown.

evidence.detail: aria-invalid set on select#arrive and on each berth radio

factor_notes.frequency: Only in the error states of two pages.
factor_notes.impact: Weaker visual cue; message text remains.

candidates.recommendation: Extend the invalid rule to select[aria-invalid="true"] and to .option:has(input[aria-invalid="true"]).

candidates.title: Chosen berth card has no selected style beyond the native radio dot
candidates.description: A selectable card should show its selected state clearly. .option has hover styling (styles.css:375-377) and the radio uses accent-color, but there is no rule for a checked card (no :has(input:checked) or equivalent) and no focus-within style on the card, so the chosen card's border, background and weight are identical to the other three.
candidates.impact: Skippers comparing four similar cards may be less sure which berth is selected before continuing, especially on small screens where the 24 px radio is the only cue.

evidence.detail: .option, .option:hover, .option input, .option input:hover/:active defined; no checked or focus-within state

factor_notes.impact: Possible hesitation; native radio dot still shows the choice.

candidates.recommendation: Add .option:has(input:checked) with an accent border and tint, and .option:has(:focus-visible) if the card should echo focus.

candidates.title: Arrival date outside the bookable season or in the past is accepted
candidates.description: Input should be checked against the constraints the page states. The date input declares min=2026-10-01 and max=2027-03-31 (index.html:45), but the form is novalidate and the submit handler only checks that a value exists (app.js:114). A typed or browser-entered date outside that range, or before today, goes through to the berth list, which then reports berths as 'free on these dates'.
candidates.impact: A skipper who mistypes the year may continue through the flow and receive a confirmation for a date the harbour does not take.

evidence.detail: only !date.value is checked; min/max and past dates are not
form novalidate disables the native min/max check

factor_notes.frequency: Only when a date outside the range is entered.

candidates.recommendation: Validate the date against min, max and today in the submit handler, with a message that states the bookable range.

candidates.title: Later steps proceed with missing upstream details and fill gaps silently
candidates.description: Each step should detect missing earlier choices. The boat step falls back to berth B14 when the berth parameter is absent (app.js:186); the review page lets 'Confirm booking' succeed while the summary still shows 'Not chosen yet' (app.js:211-227 checks only skipper and mobile); and the confirmed page then shows 'Not chosen yet' rows with the reference left as 'being prepared' (confirmed.html:34; app.js:237).
candidates.impact: A skipper arriving via a stale or edited link may receive a 'Booking confirmed' page without a berth, date or reference.

evidence.detail: submit validates only skipper and mobile before navigating to confirmed.html

factor_notes.frequency: Rare in the declared journeys, which pass every parameter; occurs on edited, bookmarked or truncated links.

candidates.recommendation: On each step, check the required upstream parameters and send the user back to the step that supplies the first missing one.

candidates.title: Tide table is in UTC while arrival times and office hours carry no time zone
candidates.description: Times a user must compare should share a time zone. The tide table caption states 'times in UTC' (index.html:79) and the copy asks skippers to plan arrival around high water (index.html:34, 94), but the arrival-time options (index.html:62-68) and harbour-office hours (footer) are bare clock times. The tabled dates (17-23 October 2026) fall in British Summer Time, when local time is UTC+1.

criteria.name: Match between system and the real world

candidates.impact: A skipper who picks an arrival time straight from the tide table may plan to arrive an hour off the sill-gate window.

locations.snippet: <caption>High water at the quay, times in UTC</caption>

factor_notes.frequency: Every skipper who uses the tide table to choose an arrival time during summer time.
factor_notes.impact: Arrival planned an hour away from the intended tide.
factor_notes.persistence: Recurs until the user notices the zone.

candidates.recommendation: Show tide times in UK local time (or label both columns and the arrival select with the same zone).
